title: Why Do Only Your Fingers Wrinkle? #body #science
description:
It isn't just your skin soaking up water. In the 1930s, doctors saw that fingers with a damaged nerve didn't wrinkle at all. The nerve signal narrows the blood vessels in the fingertip, the pad loses a little volume, and the skin folds. Why we evolved this is still debated.

Full episode: Why do your fingers wrinkle in water? https://youtu.be/dTu9m6gXCck

Sources
- Haseleu et al. (2014), PLoS ONE 9(1): e84949
- Lewis & Pickering (1936), Clinical Science 2: 149
- Wilder-Smith & Chow (2003), Microvascular Research 66: 68
- Wilder-Smith (2004), Clinical Autonomic Research 14: 125
- Kareklas, Nettle & Smulders (2013), Biology Letters 9: 20120999

subtitles: Why do only your fingers and toes wrinkle in water?
Your arms and your back stay smooth.
Only fingertips and toes turn into prunes.
Most people think the skin just soaks up water.
In the 1930s, doctors noticed something strange.
Fingers with a damaged nerve didn't wrinkle.
Here's how it seems to work.
The nerve tells blood vessels in the fingertip to narrow.
The fingertip loses a little volume, and the skin on top folds into wrinkles.
Your nervous system is making them wrinkle.
Scientists are still arguing about that.
